questions.question: Management accounting is also referred to as:

options.A: Financial reporting or external auditing
options.B: Cost accounting or controlling
options.C: Procurement accounting or sourcing
options.D: Fulfillment accounting or order-to-cash

questions.explanation: It is concerned with tracking costs and revenues for internal purposes.

questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts financial and management accounting?

options.A: Management accounting must follow GAAP or IFRS and uses only historical data
options.B: Financial accounting is geared toward internal managers and is highly flexible
options.C: Both are required to use identical methods and standards
options.D: Management accounting is more flexible, is geared toward internal users and includes forward-looking as well as historical data

questions.explanation: Financial accounting serves outside parties such as investors and regulators and follows GAAP/IFRS.

questions.question: Which consideration is important when selecting techniques used in management accounting?

options.A: The techniques must be identical to those used for financial accounting
options.B: Cost-benefit: the benefits of the analysis must outweigh the costs of capturing and analyzing the data
options.C: The techniques must be approved by external regulators
options.D: The techniques must use the same depreciation method as the tax return

questions.explanation: An organization may use a different inventory or depreciation method for management accounting.

questions.question: Which three processes are the key processes in management accounting?

options.A: Procurement, fulfillment and production
options.B: General ledger, accounts payable and accounts receivable
options.C: Product costing, overhead management and profitability analysis
options.D: Cost centers, internal orders and cost elements

questions.explanation: Chapter 3 focuses exclusively on overhead management.

questions.question: What is product costing concerned with?

options.A: Accurately tracking the costs of creating a product or service and calculating the cost of goods manufactured
options.B: Tracking and allocating indirect costs with the goal of cost containment
options.C: Evaluating the profitability of different parts of the organization
options.D: Recording the consequences of vendor invoices in the general ledger

questions.explanation: Product costs include direct and indirect costs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct cost of producing a bicycle?

options.A: The rent for the factory building
options.B: The salaries of factory supervisors
options.C: The wheels and handlebars used (material) and the time to assemble the bike (labor)
options.D: The electricity and water used in the factory

questions.explanation: Rent, utilities, repairs and supervisor salaries are indirect costs (factory overhead).

questions.question: What is the cost of goods manufactured formula in the text?

options.A: Direct material cost + direct labor cost + indirect cost
options.B: Direct material cost + selling costs + administrative costs
options.C: Revenue – direct labor cost – indirect cost
options.D: Direct labor cost + marketing cost + overhead of support departments

questions.explanation: Indirect costs are also called factory overhead.

questions.question: Which of the following is overhead of support departments that is NOT assigned to the cost of goods manufactured?

options.A: Rent of the factory where bicycles are produced
options.B: Costs of human resources, accounting, purchasing, marketing and IT departments
options.C: Repairs to production machinery in the factory
options.D: Salaries of supervisors who oversee factory operations

questions.explanation: These costs are included in accounts such as selling, general, and administrative costs.

questions.question: What does profitability analysis take into consideration that product costing and overhead management do not?

options.A: Only costs of the support departments
options.B: Only the direct material and labor
options.C: Only the costs of internal orders
options.D: Revenues in addition to costs

questions.explanation: It evaluates the profitability of different parts of the organization.

questions.question: Which process is used to track and allocate ongoing indirect costs, and which for temporary costs?

options.A: Internal order accounting for ongoing costs; cost center accounting for temporary costs
options.B: Cost center accounting for ongoing costs; internal order accounting for temporary costs
options.C: Product costing for ongoing costs; profitability analysis for temporary costs
options.D: Cost center accounting for both ongoing and temporary costs

questions.explanation: Participating in a trade show is a temporary event with finite starting and ending times.

topics.topicName: Cost centers, cost elements & controlling objects

questions.question: Why are cost centers sometimes called responsibility centers?

options.A: They are responsible for recording revenue from customer invoices
options.B: They are responsible for defining the chart of accounts of the company
options.C: They are responsible for settling the costs of internal orders
options.D: They are the organizational units most responsible for controlling (containing) the costs

questions.explanation: Cost center accounting is often called responsibility accounting.

questions.question: What are cost elements?

options.A: Organizational units that are responsible for incurring and controlling costs
options.B: Master data used to transfer costs between financial accounting and management accounting and within management accounting
options.C: Temporary events with finite starting and ending times
options.D: Values that serve as the basis for allocating costs

questions.explanation: There are two categories: primary and secondary.

questions.question: Which cost elements are associated with general ledger accounts?

options.A: Secondary cost elements
options.B: Statistical key figures
options.C: Activity types
options.D: Primary cost elements

questions.explanation: Primary cost elements transfer data between financial accounting and management accounting.

questions.question: For what are secondary cost elements used?

options.A: To transfer data within management accounting; they are not associated with G/L accounts
options.B: To transfer costs from the general ledger to cost centers
options.C: To record vendor invoices in accounts payable
options.D: To define the posting periods of the controlling area

questions.explanation: Examples: assessment and internal activity allocation.

questions.question: How are postings from financial accounting to management accounting different from postings within financial accounting?

options.A: They are two-sided, while financial accounting postings are one-sided
options.B: Both are one-sided
options.C: They are one-sided (a debit to the cost center with no corresponding credit), while financial accounting postings are two-sided
options.D: Both are two-sided but use different currencies

questions.explanation: Example: $500 debit to supplies expense and credit to bank in FI, and $500 debit to the cost center in CO.

questions.question: What is a controlling (management accounting) object?

options.A: An object in management accounting that can receive and accumulate costs and in some cases allocate costs to other objects
options.B: A general ledger account that is linked to a reconciliation account
options.C: An organizational unit that represents a separate legal entity
options.D: A document that records the allocation of costs

questions.explanation: A cost center is an example.

questions.question: Which of the following are real controlling objects?

options.A: Profit centers and statistical internal orders only
options.B: Cost elements and activity types
options.C: Cost centers, internal orders and production orders
options.D: Company codes and plants

questions.explanation: Real objects can receive real postings and can allocate costs to other objects.

questions.question: What is a statistical posting?

options.A: A posting that is included in the account balance of the object
options.B: A posting that transfers costs from financial accounting
options.C: A posting that is made only to profit centers
options.D: An additional posting made for informational or reporting purposes that is not included in the account balance of the object

questions.explanation: Statistical postings appear only in reports for the object.

questions.question: A cost is posted to an internal order (real posting) and a cost center (additional posting). What happens to the cost center?

options.A: It receives a real posting; the amount is included in its balance
options.B: It receives a statistical posting; the amount is not included in its account balance
options.C: It receives no posting at all
options.D: It receives a credit posting for the same amount

questions.explanation: The internal order receives the real posting because of the order of priority among objects.

questions.question: What is the order of priority used to determine which object receives the real posting?

options.A: Cost center, internal order, WBS element, make-to-order sales order, profitability segment
options.B: Profitability segment, make-to-order sales order, WBS element, internal order, cost center
options.C: Internal order, cost center, profitability segment, WBS element, sales order
options.D: WBS element, cost center, internal order, profitability segment, sales order

questions.explanation: Up to four objects can be specified in a posting.

questions.question: Which objects can receive only statistical postings?

options.A: Real objects such as cost centers
options.B: Real objects such as internal orders
options.C: General ledger accounts
options.D: Statistical objects such as profit centers

questions.explanation: Internal orders and projects can also be designated as statistical objects when they are created.

questions.question: How many objects can be specified in a single posting?

options.A: Only one
options.B: Up to four
options.C: Up to two
options.D: Up to ten

questions.explanation: The system uses a predefined order of priority to decide which one gets the real posting.

questions.question: What are the two techniques available for allocating costs in cost center accounting?

options.A: Distribution and settlement
options.B: Assessment and settlement
options.C: Periodic allocation and internal activity allocation
options.D: Settlement and internal activity allocation

questions.explanation: Internal order accounting uses settlement instead.

questions.question: How does periodic allocation work?

options.A: Costs are accumulated over a period (e.g., a month) and allocated to other objects at the end of the period
options.B: Costs are allocated at the moment they are incurred based on activity performed
options.C: Costs are allocated only when the order is closed
options.D: Costs are allocated once when the cost center is created

questions.explanation: Techniques include distribution and assessment.

questions.question: The distribution technique of periodic allocation is appropriate for allocating which costs?

options.A: Secondary costs only
options.B: Several costs combined into one secondary cost
options.C: Primary costs, each allocated individually
options.D: Costs of internal orders

questions.explanation: The same primary cost element is used in the distribution, so receivers can identify the source of the cost.

questions.question: What is a statistical key figure?

options.A: A document that records a statistical posting
options.B: A value that serves as the basis for allocating costs, such as the number of employees or building area
options.C: A cost element used in assessments
options.D: The rate charged for an activity type

questions.explanation: Other examples: area in square feet and miles driven.

questions.question: $5,000 of supplies cost is distributed to Departments A (10 employees), B (20 employees) and C (20 employees) based on the number of employees. How much does Department A receive?
questions.explanation: Department A has 10 of 50 employees = 20%, i.e., $1,000; B and C each receive $2,000.

questions.question: Which objects are valid senders in a distribution or an assessment?

options.A: Cost centers and internal orders
options.B: Only cost centers
options.C: Only internal orders
options.D: Cost centers, internal orders and G/L accounts

questions.explanation: Receivers can be cost centers or other real objects, but there must be at least one receiver.

questions.question: How are the sending cost center and the receivers posted in a distribution?

options.A: The sender receives a debit posting and the receivers receive credit postings
options.B: Only the receivers are posted; the sender is not posted
options.C: All objects receive statistical postings
options.D: The sender receives a credit posting and the receivers receive debit postings (double entry)

questions.explanation: Postings within management accounting use the double-entry technique.

questions.question: How does an assessment differ from a distribution?

options.A: An assessment allocates only one primary cost using the original cost element
options.B: An assessment allocates costs based on activity quantity and activity type
options.C: An assessment assigns multiple costs (primary and secondary) to receivers at the same time as a single secondary cost
options.D: An assessment settles the costs of an internal order to a G/L account

questions.explanation: In an assessment, two or more costs are combined into a secondary cost.

questions.question: Why can the receivers of an assessment not see the makeup of the allocated cost?

options.A: Because the combined costs are posted with a secondary cost element, which is not associated with a G/L account
options.B: Because assessments are posted as statistical postings only
options.C: Because the receivers are statistical objects
options.D: Because the original cost elements are deleted after the period closes

questions.explanation: The original costs lose their identity in the receiving objects.

questions.question: Which cost element category is used in the assessment technique of periodic allocation?

options.A: Primary cost element category 01
options.B: Secondary cost element category 42
options.C: Secondary cost element category 43
options.D: Secondary cost element category 21

questions.explanation: Category 43 is used for internal activity allocation; 21 for internal settlement; 22 for external settlement.

questions.question: How does internal activity allocation differ from periodic allocation?

options.A: Costs are accumulated for a period and then allocated using statistical key figures
options.B: Costs are settled to a G/L account at the end of the life of an order
options.C: Costs are allocated only to profit centers
options.D: No initial accumulation occurs; costs are allocated from a cost center based on activity performed, when they are incurred

questions.explanation: The cost center continues to receive postings independent of its allocation.

questions.question: The IT department charges $100 per hour for 12 hours of website development for marketing. What amount is charged and how is it posted?

options.A: $100: debit to the IT cost center and credit to the marketing cost center
options.B: $1,200: credit to the IT cost center (sender) and debit to the marketing cost center (receiver)
options.C: $1,200: debit to the IT cost center and credit to the marketing cost center
options.D: $1,200: statistical posting to both cost centers

questions.explanation: The allocation is a secondary cost using a secondary cost element.

questions.question: What does an activity type define?

options.A: The cost center category that determines which postings are permitted
options.B: The basis used for periodic allocation, such as number of employees
options.C: The category of cost elements used for settlement
options.D: The activity or work performed by a cost center, such as programming time charged at a rate per hour

questions.explanation: Internal activity allocation uses activity type and quantity as the basis.

questions.question: What is the allocation basis of internal activity allocation?

options.A: Activity type and quantity of activity
options.B: Statistical key figures
options.C: Equivalence numbers
options.D: Percentages defined in distribution rules

questions.explanation: Periodic allocations use statistical key figures.

questions.question: Which cost element category is used for internal activity allocation?

options.A: Primary cost element category 01
options.B: Secondary cost element category 42
options.C: Secondary cost element category 43
options.D: Primary cost element category 22

questions.explanation: Internal activity allocation is for a secondary cost using a secondary cost element.

questions.question: What is internal order accounting used to manage?

options.A: Ongoing costs such as rent, utilities and purchasing
options.B: The cost of goods manufactured for each product
options.C: Temporary costs associated with an activity that has a finite life, such as a trade show or picnic
options.D: The allocation of costs using statistical key figures

questions.explanation: Internal orders are the initial cost collectors for these temporary events.

questions.question: Which technique does internal order accounting use to allocate accumulated costs?

options.A: Settlement
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Distribution
options.D: Internal activity allocation

questions.explanation: Settlement transfers costs from the internal order to other controlling objects or G/L accounts.

questions.question: What happens when an internal order is closed?

options.A: It can still receive costs but they are posted statistically
options.B: It is deleted from the system
options.C: It cannot receive any further costs
options.D: Its costs are automatically settled to a profit center

questions.explanation: The order is closed after the event is complete and the costs are settled.

questions.question: What does a settlement rule indicate?

options.A: Which general ledger accounts can be posted to by the order
options.B: How the costs accumulated in the internal order will be allocated among the receivers
options.C: Which strategy sequence the system uses to determine the posting key
options.D: Which cost elements are used to allocate costs in cost centers

questions.explanation: It is defined when the internal order is created.

questions.question: What does each distribution rule specify?

options.A: A sender, a posting key and a document type
options.B: A cost center, an activity type and a quantity
options.C: A company code, a currency and a language
options.D: A receiver, an amount (percentage or equivalence number) and the timing of settlement

questions.explanation: A settlement rule consists of one or more distribution rules.

questions.question: Two cost centers are to receive 2/3 and 1/3 of the costs of an internal order. Which equivalence numbers are specified?

options.A: 2 and 3
options.B: 2 and 1
options.C: 1 and 1
options.D: 66 and 33

questions.explanation: The first rule allocates 2/3 and the second 1/3.

questions.question: What are the three categories of settlement receivers for internal orders?

options.A: Cost center, profit center and company code
options.B: Controlling area, plant and cost element
options.C: Vendor, customer and G/L account
options.D: Cost center, general ledger account and another order

questions.explanation: The valid receivers are determined by the settlement profile.

questions.question: What are the two options for the timing of settlement?

options.A: Daily and monthly
options.B: Partial and complete
options.C: Periodic and full
options.D: Manual and automatic

questions.explanation: Periodic settles at the end of each period; full settles once at the end of the order's life.

questions.question: In "full" settlement timing, when are the costs settled?

options.A: Once, at the end of the life of the order
options.B: At the end of each period in which the order is open
options.C: Every time a cost is posted to the order
options.D: When the order is created

questions.explanation: In periodic settlement, costs are settled at the end of each period the order is open.

questions.question: An internal order tracks the cost of constructing a building and is settled to an asset account in financial accounting. What type of settlement is this?

options.A: Internal settlement
options.B: External settlement
options.C: Periodic allocation
options.D: Internal activity allocation

questions.explanation: Internal settlement is to another object within controlling, e.g., a cost center.

questions.question: Which cost element category is used in external settlement from an internal order to financial accounting?

options.A: Secondary cost element category 21
options.B: Secondary cost element category 42
options.C: Primary cost element category 01
options.D: Primary cost element category 22

questions.explanation: Category 21 is used for settlement to receivers within management accounting.

questions.question: Which cost element category is used to transfer costs from financial accounting to cost centers and internal orders?

options.A: Primary cost element category 22
options.B: Primary cost element category 01
options.C: Secondary cost element category 42
options.D: Secondary cost element category 43

questions.explanation: Category 01 is the standard primary cost element category.

questions.question: Which enterprise structure elements are relevant to management accounting?

options.A: Company code and controlling area
options.B: Plant and storage location
options.C: Sales organization and distribution channel
options.D: Purchasing organization and purchasing group

questions.explanation: The controlling area is the key element for management accounting.

questions.question: At which level are overhead management and product costing processes completed?

options.A: At the plant level
options.B: At the client level
options.C: At the controlling area level
options.D: At the company code level only

questions.explanation: All costs in management accounting are allocated within a controlling area.

questions.question: How is a controlling area identified?

options.A: By a unique four-character alphanumeric value, a descriptive name and optionally the person responsible
options.B: By a two-digit numeric code assigned to each company code
options.C: By a ten-digit number that falls within an account group range
options.D: By the language and country of the company code

questions.explanation: GBI's North America controlling area is NA00.

questions.question: What is the centralized model of controlling called in the assignment control parameter?

options.A: Controlling area same as company code
options.B: Parallel cost accounting
options.C: Plant-level cost accounting
options.D: Cross-company-code cost accounting

questions.explanation: Several company codes are assigned to the same controlling area (a 1:n relationship).

questions.question: What does the option "controlling area same as company code" create?

options.A: A one-to-many relationship between a controlling area and several company codes
options.B: A one-to-one (1:1) relationship between each controlling area and company code (decentralized model)
options.C: A many-to-many relationship between cost centers and internal orders
options.D: A hybrid with no company code assignment

questions.explanation: Organizations typically choose the centralized option because it is easier to configure and offers more flexible analysis.

questions.question: What is required in a centralized model of controlling between the controlling area and its assigned company codes?

options.A: They must use the same currency and the same language
options.B: They must have the same number of cost centers
options.C: They must be located in the same country
options.D: They must use the same fiscal year variant and the same chart of accounts

questions.explanation: Controlling areas, like company codes, are assigned a chart of accounts and fiscal year variant.

questions.question: Which currency is the currency the organization uses for all of its management accounting activity?

options.A: Object currency
options.B: Controlling area currency
options.C: Transaction currency
options.D: Country currency

questions.explanation: In a decentralized model it equals the company code currency.

questions.question: What is the object currency?

options.A: The currency associated with a controlling object such as a cost center or an internal order
options.B: The currency used when posting controlling transactions
options.C: The currency used for all management accounting
options.D: The currency of the company code that owns the object

questions.explanation: It can differ from the company code currency only if the controlling area currency and company code currency are the same.

questions.question: What is the transaction currency in controlling?

options.A: The currency of the controlling area only
options.B: The currency of the company code only
options.C: The currency used when posting controlling transactions, which need not be the controlling area or object currency
options.D: The currency of the cost center hierarchy

questions.explanation: Example: research costs incurred in China and Germany posted in yuan and euros.

questions.question: What does the cost center standard hierarchy contain?

options.A: Only the cost centers that have internal orders assigned
options.B: All cost centers of the organization; every cost center must belong to it
options.C: Only the cost centers of one company code
options.D: Only the cost center groups, not the cost centers

questions.explanation: Alternate hierarchies can be created for reporting, but each cost center must be in the standard hierarchy.

questions.question: Why must company codes be assigned to the controlling area?

options.A: So that the controlling area can define its own chart of accounts
options.B: So that each company code can create its own cost elements
options.C: So that internal orders can be created without number ranges
options.D: So that expense and revenue postings in financial accounting can be posted to the appropriate controlling objects

questions.explanation: Management accounting receives much of its data from financial accounting.

topics.topicName: Number ranges, settlement parameters & order types

questions.question: Document number ranges in controlling are unique to which element?

options.A: Each company code
options.B: Each controlling area
options.C: Each cost center
options.D: The whole client

questions.explanation: Number ranges must also be defined for internal orders and settlement documents.

questions.question: What does the "Ext" checkbox of a number range specify?

options.A: Whether the number range extends into the next fiscal year
options.B: Whether the number range is shared with other company codes
options.C: Whether the documents can be reversed
options.D: Whether the number is selected manually by the user (checked) or automatically by the system (unchecked)

questions.explanation: Other parameters: interval number, from/to numbers and NR status (last number used).

questions.question: Which three categories of settlement parameters determine how costs are allocated to other controlling objects?

options.A: Number ranges, order types and strategy sequences
options.B: Allocation structures, source structures and settlement profiles
options.C: Cost elements, cost centers and activity types
options.D: Posting keys, document types and field statuses

questions.explanation: The settlement profile is the critical parameter that gathers the others.

questions.question: What does an allocation structure identify?

options.A: The sequence in which strategies are evaluated for generating settlement rules
options.B: The purpose and number range of an internal order
options.C: The type and source of costs to be included, the method of settlement and the valid types of receivers
options.D: The numbers of employees used as an allocation basis

questions.explanation: Examples: A3 for customer service, A4 for enterprise asset management, Z1 for internal orders.

questions.question: What do assignments in an allocation structure identify?

options.A: The types of costs or revenues to be accumulated and settled
options.B: The cost centers that are valid receivers
options.C: The strategy used to generate a settlement rule
options.D: The statuses that an internal order can have

questions.explanation: They can include primary costs, secondary costs and revenue.

questions.question: An allocation structure uses assessment cost elements to settle costs. What does that mean?

options.A: Each cost keeps its original cost element during settlement
options.B: The costs are settled to a G/L account only
options.C: All the costs are combined into a single secondary cost element
options.D: The costs are posted statistically

questions.explanation: Settlement cost elements allow multiple options depending on the receiver category.

questions.question: Which source structure statement is true?

options.A: It identifies the source of the costs to be settled and can be embedded in an allocation structure or defined standalone
options.B: It defines the receivers that are valid for an internal order
options.C: It defines the number range of internal orders
options.D: It can only be defined inside a settlement profile

questions.explanation: A standalone source structure is more general and can be used in multiple scenarios.

questions.question: What does a settlement profile do?

options.A: It defines the strategy sequence for creating cost elements
options.B: It defines numerous settlement parameters that the internal order inherits when the profile is assigned to it
options.C: It defines the fiscal year variant of the controlling area
options.D: It defines the posting keys used by the internal order

questions.explanation: Its parameters are grouped into type of settlement, default values, allocation basis, valid receivers and other parameters.

questions.question: If the type of settlement is "full settlement", what happens when a user tries to close an order that has a balance?

options.A: The system closes the order and displays a warning
options.B: The system closes the order and posts the balance to a cost center
options.C: The system leaves the order open without any message
options.D: The system generates an error because the order must have a zero balance

questions.explanation: With the "can be settled" option, the system displays a warning but permits closing.

questions.question: What does the type of settlement "not for settlement" indicate?

options.A: The order must be fully settled before closing
options.B: The order should not be settled
options.C: The order can be settled but need not be
options.D: The order is settled automatically each period

questions.explanation: The three options: full settlement required, can be settled, not for settlement.

questions.question: What does the 100%-validation option of a settlement profile do?

options.A: It forces every order to be settled in one period
options.B: It requires every cost center to receive 100% of the costs
options.C: It validates that the order has a balance of 100
options.D: It makes the system verify that the percentages in the distribution rules total 100

questions.explanation: This ensures all of the costs are settled.

questions.question: What does the "maximum number of distribution rules" parameter specify?

options.A: The number of orders permitted for each cost center
options.B: The number of distribution rules permitted in a settlement rule
options.C: The number of receivers permitted in each company code
options.D: The number of periods in which an order can be settled

questions.explanation: In the GBI example 10 distribution rules are permitted.

questions.question: Strategies for automatically generating settlement rules determine:

options.A: The priority and sequence in which strategies are evaluated
options.B: The status of the order
options.C: The number range of the order
options.D: Which receivers to include in the distribution rules

questions.explanation: The strategy sequence gives the priority and sequence in which strategies are evaluated.

questions.question: What does a strategy sequence indicate?

options.A: The priority and sequence in which to evaluate whether a particular strategy is applicable
options.B: Which receivers to include in distribution rules
options.C: Which number range the order uses
options.D: Which statuses are permitted for the order

questions.explanation: Example: SAP030 determines the requesting cost center and generates a 100% periodic rule.

questions.question: Why are separate internal order types defined?

options.A: Because each order type has its own company code and chart of accounts
options.B: Because order types determine which accounts are balance sheet accounts
options.C: Each purpose (e.g., construction, marketing, picnic) has different parameters, and an order type simplifies the creation of actual orders
options.D: Because order types define the controlling area currency

questions.explanation: An order type is associated with parameters such as number range, settlement profile and strategy sequence.

questions.question: What is a model order?

options.A: An order created based on the internal order type that contains default values and serves as the basis for creating internal orders
options.B: An order that is settled to a model cost center
options.C: An order that has been closed and archived
options.D: An order that is used only for statistical postings

questions.explanation: Object class and responsible cost center come from the model order.

questions.question: Which internal order status permits planning activities only?

options.A: Released
options.B: Technically complete
options.C: Created
options.D: Closed

questions.explanation: In the Released status logistics activities are permitted.

questions.question: Which statuses of an internal order allow the order to be settled?

options.A: Created only
options.B: Closed only
options.C: Created and closed
options.D: Technically complete (settlement is possible); it cannot be settled when closed

questions.explanation: The order is closed after settlement; no further activities are permitted afterwards.

topics.topicName: Master data: cost centers, cost element groups & categories

questions.question: What are cost centers created based on?

options.A: Company code, plant and storage location
options.B: Posting period, fiscal year and document type
options.C: Material type, vendor and customer
options.D: Geographic location, function or activity

questions.explanation: Examples: the copy center, security department and IT function.

questions.question: What are cost center groups used for?

options.A: Grouping cost elements for allocation to internal orders
options.B: Grouping cost centers with similar characteristics to provide additional structure for the cost center hierarchy
options.C: Grouping controlling areas for consolidation
options.D: Grouping settlement rules for automatic generation

questions.explanation: Each group can include subgroups; the standard hierarchy is like a tree with cost centers at the lowest level.

questions.question: What does the cost center category indicate?

options.A: Which person is responsible for the cost center
options.B: Which controlling area the cost center belongs to
options.C: Which company code the cost center is assigned to
options.D: Which types of postings (e.g., primary and secondary costs) are permitted to the cost center; it is also used for reporting

questions.explanation: Other cost center data: name, status, validity dates, person responsible and department.

questions.question: How are primary cost elements typically named relative to the associated G/L account?

options.A: They have the same number, name and description as the associated G/L account
options.B: They have a different number range from the G/L accounts
options.C: They have no association with G/L accounts
options.D: They use the group chart of accounts

questions.explanation: Example: account and cost element 740000 Supplies Expense.

questions.question: What is a cost element group used for?

options.A: Combining cost centers into a hierarchy
options.B: Combining company codes assigned to the same controlling area
options.C: Combining cost elements with similar characteristics to make tracking and cost control more efficient
options.D: Combining internal orders of the same type

questions.explanation: GBI has groups for salary and wages, utilities and tax-related expenses.

questions.question: What does the default account assignment of a cost element do?

options.A: Automatically posts an expense to a specified cost center or internal order when the G/L account is posted
options.B: Automatically creates the G/L account for the cost element
options.C: Automatically settles the internal order at the end of the period
options.D: Automatically assigns the controlling area to the company code

questions.explanation: It is optional.

questions.question: What does a statistical key figure serve as in periodic allocation?

options.A: The rate charged per activity unit
options.B: The receiver of a distribution
options.C: The allocation basis, such as number of employees
options.D: The category of a cost element

questions.explanation: Statistical key figures are master data used for periodic allocation.

questions.question: Which master data are listed as relevant for overhead management?

options.A: Material master, vendor master, customer master, BOM and routing
options.B: G/L accounts, document types, posting keys and number ranges
options.C: Plants, storage locations, purchasing groups and sales areas
options.D: Cost elements, cost centers, activity types, statistical key figures and internal orders

questions.explanation: Cost elements move data between objects; activity types are for internal activity allocation.

questions.question: The costs of repairing equipment are accumulated in a maintenance order and then settled to the cost center that owns the equipment. Which concept does this illustrate?

options.A: Settlement applies only to internal orders created for events
options.B: Settlement applies in other management accounting processes such as enterprise asset management
options.C: Periodic allocation applies to enterprise asset management
options.D: Statistical postings are made to maintenance orders

questions.explanation: The same settlement techniques are used for service orders in customer service.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Management Accounting (CO)?

options.A: To meet the legal requirements of a country or reporting standard
options.B: To record all monetary flows and evaluate the inventories
options.C: To collect revenue and expenses by areas of responsibility and provide information for management decisions
options.D: To produce the balance sheet for external stakeholders

questions.explanation: CO covers all functions necessary for controlling costs and revenues effectively.

questions.question: Which is the primary source of data for CO?

options.A: Financial Accounting (FI): most expense postings in the G/L result in a cost posting in CO
options.B: Human Capital Management, which posts all labor costs to CO
options.C: Sales order management, which posts all revenue to CO
options.D: Production planning, which posts all production costs to CO

questions.explanation: Expense postings can be journal postings, vendor invoices or depreciation postings.

questions.question: What does Product Cost Controlling calculate?

options.A: The profit or loss of an organization per market segment
options.B: The costs that occur at the cost centers for each period
options.C: The costs incurred when a service is provided or a product is manufactured, e.g., the minimum price for profitable marketing
options.D: The costs that are collected for temporary internal activities

questions.explanation: BOMs and routings can be used in CO-PC.

questions.question: What does Profitability Analysis (CO-PA) do?

options.A: Calculates the cost of manufacturing a product or service
options.B: Analyzes profit or loss per market segment by assigning costs to the revenues of each segment
options.C: Allocates costs between cost centers and internal orders
options.D: Records the depreciation of fixed assets in the G/L

questions.explanation: It gives a basis for calculating prices, targeting customers and choosing sales channels.

questions.question: What does Cost Center Accounting take the costs of a company and do with them?

options.A: Assigns them to the market segments with the highest revenue
options.B: Posts them to the balance sheet accounts of the company code
options.C: Combines them in one internal order for the period
options.D: Allocates them to the sub-areas that actually caused them

questions.explanation: Cost centers are separate areas within a controlling area at which costs are incurred.

questions.question: In cost center accounting, what is the role of an activity type?

options.A: The category of a cost element used in assessments
options.B: The type of activity that can be provided by a cost center, valued with a price
options.C: The hierarchy node a cost center belongs to
options.D: The profit center to which a cost center is assigned

questions.explanation: Activity outputs supplied by one cost center to others represent a utilization of resources.

questions.question: What are internal orders used for?

options.A: To record the costs of customer orders for billing
options.B: To post the depreciation of fixed assets to the G/L
options.C: To group cost centers with similar characteristics
options.D: To plan, collect and analyze the costs arising from internal activities

questions.explanation: Internal orders can settle costs to cost centers, ABC processes and other internal orders.

questions.question: Which statement describes the difference between FI and CO regarding the level at which they are needed?

options.A: The level for CO is determined by law; FI analyzes costs worldwide
options.B: Both are determined by law and identical in every country
options.C: The level for FI is determined by law and differs per country; CO analyzes costs and revenues across country boundaries
options.D: Neither is limited by legal reporting requirements

questions.explanation: Results in Management Accounting can be compared with those in FI (reconciliation).

questions.question: What is the Universal Journal in SAP S/4HANA, and what is its table?

options.A: The common line item store of actual data for FI and CO, table ACDOCA
options.B: The list of all journal entry templates, table BKPF
options.C: The header table of accounting documents, table BSEG
options.D: The table of controlling objects, table COSP

questions.explanation: It is the single source of truth for all accounting components.

questions.question: Which benefits does the Universal Journal data model provide?

options.A: One line item table with full detail, data stored only once so no reconciliation is needed, and fast multi-dimensional reporting without replication to BI
options.B: Separate tables for FI and CO that are reconciled every night
options.C: Aggregated totals only, to reduce the memory footprint
options.D: Replication of all postings to BI for every report

questions.explanation: It also reduces the memory footprint through elimination of redundancy.

questions.question: What is a cost center?

options.A: A management-oriented unit used for internal profit control
options.B: A temporary object that collects the costs of an event
options.C: A G/L account that records the costs of a department
options.D: Master data in a CO area representing a delimited location where costs occur

questions.explanation: It supports cost determination and cost controlling.

questions.question: According to which approaches can cost centers be defined?

options.A: Only by the legal entity (company code) they belong to
options.B: Functional requirements, allocation criteria, activities and services provided, geographic location or area of responsibility
options.C: Only by the product groups that they produce
options.D: Only by the customers they supply with services

questions.explanation: The approach should be consistent throughout the enterprise.

questions.question: What must each CO area have regarding cost centers?

options.A: A separate standard hierarchy for each company code
options.B: A profit center for every cost center created
options.C: One cost center for each G/L account
options.D: A unique standard hierarchy that includes every cost center of the CO area

questions.explanation: The standard hierarchy node field in the cost center master data must be filled.

questions.question: Which organizational area is a cost center mostly assigned to?

options.A: A profit center (its responsible organizational area)
options.B: A plant
options.C: A sales area
options.D: A purchasing group

questions.explanation: Segments can be derived via the profit center entered in the cost center master record.

questions.question: What is the cost center master record in terms of time?

options.A: Valid for all periods and assigned directly to the company code
options.B: Valid only for one fiscal year and deleted at year end
options.C: Time dependent and assigned to a node of the standard cost center hierarchy
options.D: Independent of the standard hierarchy

questions.explanation: The control data can lock the cost center against planning and posting.

questions.question: What are statistical key figures?

options.A: Non-monetary information planned and posted on cost centers, used for reporting and as distribution factors
options.B: Monetary amounts allocated from one cost center to another
options.C: Secondary cost elements used in assessments
options.D: Prices valuing the activity types of a cost center

questions.explanation: Example: distributing facility costs by the square meters used.

questions.question: What does the category "Fixed" mean for a statistical key figure?

options.A: Periodic values can be added to a total
options.B: The value cannot be changed after posting
options.C: Periodic values cannot be added; the total of a period is calculated as the average of single values
options.D: The value is the same for all cost centers

questions.explanation: With category "Total" the periodic values can be added to a total.

questions.question: What is Profit Center Accounting (PCA) used for?

options.A: Calculating the cost of manufacturing a product
options.B: Recording all legal financial transactions of a company code
options.C: Tracking costs at the location where they occur
options.D: Evaluating specific areas of the organization, e.g., by region, function or product, to analyze internal profit and loss

questions.explanation: Typical questions: contribution of a unit, return on investment, cost management.

questions.question: What is a profit center?

options.A: A delimited location where costs occur
options.B: A management-oriented organizational unit used for internal control, essentially a company within the company
options.C: A temporary collector of costs of an event
options.D: The smallest unit with a legal set of books

questions.explanation: It is defined at CO area level and its master data is time dependent.

questions.question: What makes profit centers unique among account assignment objects?

options.A: They can be assigned to balance sheet transactions as well as to profit and loss transactions
options.B: They can only receive revenue postings
options.C: They can only be assigned to cost centers
options.D: They can be created without a controlling area

questions.explanation: Online document splitting provides balance sheet reporting at profit center level.

questions.question: Which objects have fields for profit center assignment in their master records?

options.A: Only cost centers and internal orders
options.B: Only G/L accounts and company codes
options.C: Cost centers, business processes, internal orders, projects, production orders and cost objects
options.D: Only plants and storage locations

questions.explanation: When the original object is posted, the system automatically posts to the profit center.

questions.question: Do profitability segments have a master record?

options.A: No: a profitability segment combines characteristics such as customer, product, plant or distribution channel, and the profit center is always one of them
options.B: Yes: they are master data defined at controlling area level
options.C: Yes: they are assigned to a fixed asset in the master record
options.D: No: they are posted only to the standard hierarchy node

questions.explanation: The profit center can be derived from the material and plant.
